newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch-Belgian Fortis 1996 profits rise 16 percent.
newsitem.headline: Dutch-Belgian Fortis 1996 profits rise 16 percent.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial services group Fortis posted a 16 percent increase in 1996 net profit to 731 million Ecus from 631 million in 1995 and said earnings per share would rise further in 1997.
The company declined to give a more precise forecast for 1997, but said its aim was to achieve annual profit growth of seven to 12 percent until 2000.

"It was an excellent year," co-chairman Hans Bartelds told a news conference, although results from Dutch health insurance activities had been disappointing and banking operations were hit by exceptional charges linked to the introduction of the euro and restructuring its Belgian units.
Fortis Amev, the Dutch parent company of the Fortis group, saw earnings per share rise by 15 percent to 4.42 guilders from 3.85 guilders.
Fortis AG, the Belgian parent, showed a similar increase of earnings per share to 355 Belgian francs from 310 francs.

Operating profit from insurance activities increased by 16 percent to 740 million Ecus. The group's banking result slipped 3 percent to 519 million Ecus as provisions and charges rose 16 percent to 1.63 billion Ecus.
"This (banking result) was above expectations," Bartelds told a news conference on the group's profit.

Banking results were hit by a 64 million Ecus charge to cover the cost of the switchover to a single European currency and to update computer systems to cope with the date change in the year 2000. Fortis also booked exceptional charges linked to the merger, due to be formalised this year, of Belgian banking units ASLK-CGER and NMKN-SNCI.
Fortis AG chairman Maurice Lippens, speaking separately in Brussels, said Fortis was still discussing with the Belgian government about increasing its 50 percent stake in ASLK-CGER.
Lippens reiterated the group was "pro-actively" looking for external growth opportunities, as well as seeking to maintain internal growth.
Bartelds said Fortis had also put aside 92 million Ecus for its insurance operations, which would meet the same changes due to the arrival of the euro and the millennium.
Bartelds said its recently acquired merchant banking unit MeesPierson would contribute to the groups profit in 1997.
"The impact from MeesPierson on our banking results will be noticeable from the first quarter in 1997," he said.
Fortis said it had paid goodwill of 400 million Ecus for MeesPierson, which was bought from Dutch bank ABN-AMRO at the end of December.
"Part of this was to cover for (MeesPierson's) hidden reserves," he said.
The Dutch parent of Fortis said its total hidden reserves mounted to 192 million Ecus at the end of 1996.
Bartelds said its health insurance activities in the United States and Belgium, which had both shown a loss during the last quarter of 1995, were back in the black.
"It is also extraordinary that our car insurance portfolio is profitable in all countries we work in," he said.
Fortis Amev shares ended unchanged at 71.50 guilders on the news. Belgian Fortis AG shares rose 70 francs to 6,060 francs.
